subject: english
stem: Asked about the mistake, the cadet gave a candid answer. As used here, "candid" most nearly means
rationale: Candid means frank and truthful, saying things openly. A candid answer may also be short or blunt, but neither is the meaning of the word.

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct word: One of my friends ___ a pilot.
rationale: The subject is "one", which is singular, so the verb is "is". "Friends" is plural but only describes which group the one belongs to.

subject: english
stem: Hand is to glove as foot is to ___
rationale: A glove is worn on the hand to cover it; a sock is worn on the foot. A toe is part of the foot and walking is what it does.

subject: english
stem: In a code, PEN is written as QFO. How is INK written in the same code?
rationale: Each letter moves one step forward: P→Q, E→F, N→O. So I→J, N→O, K→L, giving JOL. HMJ moves each letter back instead.

subject: english
stem: Every pilot in the squadron has passed the night-flying test. Arjun has not passed the night-flying test. Which statement must be true?

options.A: Arjun will pass the test later
options.B: Arjun is not a pilot in the squadron
options.C: Arjun is a pilot in the squadron
options.D: No pilot in the squadron flies by day

rationale: If Arjun were a pilot in the squadron he would have passed the test. He has not, so he is not one. Nothing is said about the future.

subject: maths
stem: If A = {2, 4, 6} and B = {4, 6, 8, 10}, how many elements are there in A ∪ B?
rationale: A ∪ B = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, which has 5 elements. Adding 3 + 4 = 7 counts 4 and 6 twice. This is a type-in question.

subject: maths
stem: How many radians is an angle of 90°?
rationale: 180° is π radians, so 90° is half of that: π/2. π is a straight angle and 2π a full turn.

subject: maths
stem: How many two-letter arrangements, with no letter repeated, can be made from the letters A, B, C and D?
rationale: The first letter has 4 choices and the second 3, so ⁴P₂ = 4 × 3 = 12. Counting AB and BA as one gives 6, the number of selections.

subject: maths
stem: What is the 6th term of the geometric progression 5, 10, 20, …?
rationale: The nth term is arⁿ⁻¹ = 5 × 2⁵ = 160. 320 uses 2⁶, one doubling too many; 80 stops one too early.

subject: maths
stem: What is the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (1 + x)⁵?
rationale: The term in x² is ⁵C₂ x² = 10x², so the coefficient is 10. ⁵C₂ = 5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 10. This is a type-in question.

subject: science
stem: A car speeds up uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 4 seconds. How far does it travel in that time, in metres?
rationale: Its average speed is (0 + 20) ÷ 2 = 10 m/s, so in 4 s it covers 40 m. Using the final speed for the whole time gives 80 m.

subject: science
stem: What is the mass of 0.5 mol of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16)
rationale: The molar mass of CO₂ is 12 + 2 × 16 = 44 g/mol, so 0.5 mol is 22 g. 44 g is a whole mole; 88 g multiplies by 2 instead of halving.

subject: science
stem: Which of these elements, all in Group 1, has the largest atomic radius?
rationale: Atomic radius increases down a group, as each element adds a new shell of electrons. Rubidium is lowest of the four, so it is largest.

subject: science
stem: A 1,000 kg car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest in 5 seconds. What average braking force acts on it?
rationale: Force = change in momentum ÷ time = (1000 × 20) ÷ 5 = 4,000 N. 100,000 N multiplies by the time instead of dividing.

subject: science
stem: A motor lifts a 50 kg load through 10 m in 5 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s², what power does it deliver, in watts?
rationale: Work done = mgh = 50 × 10 × 10 = 5,000 J; power = work ÷ time = 5,000 ÷ 5 = 1,000 W. This is a type-in question.
